Twenty Five of them visited all the three places while 200 visited exactly one of the three places. The number of students, who visited exactly 2 out of the three places, is five times as many as those who have not visited any of the places.

answer.explanation:
1. Total no of students = 315
\(a+b+c+x+y+z+t+r=315\)
\(200+5r+25+r=315\)
\(6r=90\Rightarrow r=15\)
\(	herefore\) 15 did not visit any of the three places. Choice (D)

answer.explanation: 2. Number of students who did not visit more than one place = Number of students who visited exactly one place + those who did not visit any = \(a+b+c+r=200+15=215\). Choice (D)

question.text: How many workers are members of only Viram or only Be-kam?
question.direction:
Directions for questions 10 to 12: These questions are based on the following data.

There are three trade unions - Viram, Vishram and Be-kam - and three thousand six hundred workers in a company. Becoming a member of a trade union is optional. A worker can be a member of more than one of the three trade unions also. There are 500 workers who are members of at least two trade unions while Vishram has 1400 members. There are 100 workers who are members of only Viram and Be-kam, whereas 200 Vishram members also are Be-kam members; 550 workers are members of only Be-kam, whereas 20% of Viram members are members of exactly one more union. An eighth of all the workers in the company are members of exactly two unions.

question.text: If 10 workers give up their Be-kam membership and take up Vishram membership, then how many workers will now have membership of all the three unions?
question.direction:
Directions for questions 10 to 12: These questions are based on the following data.

There are three trade unions - Viram, Vishram and Be-kam - and three thousand six hundred workers in a company. Becoming a member of a trade union is optional. A worker can be a member of more than one of the three trade unions also. There are 500 workers who are members of at least two trade unions while Vishram has 1400 members. There are 100 workers who are members of only Viram and Be-kam, whereas 200 Vishram members also are Be-kam members; 550 workers are members of only Be-kam, whereas 20% of Viram members are members of exactly one more union. An eighth of all the workers in the company are members of exactly two unions.

answer.explanation: 11. Since 10 workers have given up their Be-kam membership and taken up Vishram membership, it means these 10 workers were initially Be-kam members but not Vishram members, i.e., they must be a part of \(r\) or \(w\). When they give up Be-kam and take up Vishram, they will move to \(q\) or \(u\) respectively. So, \(s\) does not undergo any change at all. Hence, 50 is the answer. Choice (B)

question.text: What percent of the students passed in exactly one of the two subjects – English and the foreign language?
question.direction:
Directions for questions 13 to 15: These questions are based on the following data.

In a school, 60% of the students passed in English, and 25% of the students who passed in English passed in the foreign language also, whereas 66 rac{2}{3}\% of the students who passed in the foreign language failed in English. Twenty students failed in both English and the foreign language.

question.text: The students who failed in exactly one subject are allowed to take a re-exam and it was found that the number of students who passed in both the subjects increased by 20%. What is the least value for the percentage of students in the school who pass only in English?
question.direction:
Directions for questions 13 to 15: These questions are based on the following data.

In a school, 60% of the students passed in English, and 25% of the students who passed in English passed in the foreign language also, whereas 66 rac{2}{3}\% of the students who passed in the foreign language failed in English. Twenty students failed in both English and the foreign language.

answer.explanation: 14. 20% of 15% = 3% increase in pass in both subjects. Hence, least value of pass only in English will come when all the new people who pass in both subjects are from the group which passed only in English. i.e., 45 − 3 = 42%. Choice (A)

question.text: All the students, who failed in one or more subjects, are given grace marks and it was found that the number of students passing in exactly one subject went up by 4 and the number of students who failed in both the subjects dropped by 40%. What percent of the school now pass in both subjects?
question.direction:
Directions for questions 13 to 15: These questions are based on the following data.

In a school, 60% of the students passed in English, and 25% of the students who passed in English passed in the foreign language also, whereas 66 rac{2}{3}\% of the students who passed in the foreign language failed in English. Twenty students failed in both English and the foreign language.

answer.explanation: 15. 40% of 20 students = 8 students. Out of this, 4 students passed in exactly one subject. Hence, the remaining 4 students (which is 2% of the school strength) pass in both subjects. So, pass in both the subjects = 15 + 2 = 17%. Choice (D)

question.text: The angle between the two hands of a clock at 9:00 a.m. is 90°. What will the angle between them be one minute later?
question.direction: Directions for questions 16 to 35: Select the correct alternative from the given choices.

answer.explanation: As the minute hand is 5.5°/minute faster than the hour hand and the minute hand is ahead of the hour hand, the angle after one minute, i.e., at 9:01 a.m., will be 90° + 5.5° = 95.5°. Choice (B)

question.text: The angle between the two hands of a clock at 5:00 p.m. is 150°, what will the angle between them be one minute later?
question.direction: Directions for questions 16 to 35: Select the correct alternative from the given choices.

answer.explanation: The angle between the hands will change by 5.5°/min. In this case, since the minute hand is behind the hour hand the angle will decrease by 5.5°. Hence, the angle at 5:01 = 150 − 5.5 = 144.5°. Choice (A)

question.text: What is the angle between the two hands of a clock at 7:28 p.m.?
question.direction: Directions for questions 16 to 35: Select the correct alternative from the given choices.

answer.explanation: The angle = \(\left| rac{11}{2}(28)-30(7)ight|=56^\circ\). Choice (A)

question.text: A watch, which gains uniformly was observed to be 10 minutes slow at 12 noon and 5 minutes fast at 6:00 p.m. on the same day. When did the watch show the correct time?
question.direction: Directions for questions 16 to 35: Select the correct alternative from the given choices.

answer.explanation: In 6 hours, the watch gained 15 minutes. ∴ In order to gain 10 minutes, (the initial difference) it takes 4 hours. ∴ At 4:00 p.m. it shows the correct time. Choice (C)

question.text: A watch, which loses uniformly was observed to be 5 minutes fast at 5:00 p.m. and 4 minutes slow at 8:00 p.m. on the same day. When did the watch show the correct time?
question.direction: Directions for questions 16 to 35: Select the correct alternative from the given choices.

answer.explanation: In 3 hours, the watch loses 9 minutes. ∴ In order to lose 5 minutes, (the initial difference) it takes \(5	imes3/9\) hours, i.e., 1 hour 40 minutes. ∴ At 6:40 p.m., it shows the correct time. Choice (B)

question.text: Two clocks show the correct time at 3:00 p.m. One clock gains 4 minutes in an hour, while the other loses 4 minutes. At 6:00 p.m. on the same day, by how much time will the two clocks differ?
question.direction: Directions for questions 16 to 35: Select the correct alternative from the given choices.

answer.explanation: In one hour, the clocks will differ by (4 + 4) minutes i.e., 8 minutes. ∴ In three hours they will differ by 24 minutes. Choice (D)

question.text: The minutes hand of a clock overtakes the hours hand after every 60 minutes of correct time. How much time does the clock gain or lose in eleven hours of normal time?
question.direction: Directions for questions 16 to 35: Select the correct alternative from the given choices.

answer.explanation: As \(60<65 rac{5}{11}\), the watch is gaining time. The gain is \(65 rac{5}{11}-60=5 rac{5}{11}\) minutes per hour. ∴ In eleven hours, the watch will gain \(11\left( rac{60}{11}ight)=60\) minutes. Choice (C)

question.text: If the time in a clock is 8 hours 20 minutes, then what time does its mirror image show?
question.direction: Directions for questions 16 to 35: Select the correct alternative from the given choices.

answer.explanation: Actual time + mirror image time = 12 hours. ∴ Mirror image time = 12 − 8:20 = 3:40 = 3 hours 40 minutes. Choice (C)

question.text: If 22nd April, 1982 was a Thursday, then what day of the week was 3rd November, 1982?
question.direction: Directions for questions 16 to 35: Select the correct alternative from the given choices.

answer.explanation: It is given that 22nd April, 1982 was a Thursday. Number of days from 22nd April 1982 to 3rd November 1982. Month: April + May + June + July + August + September + October + November. In each month number of odd days: 1 + 3 + 2 + 3 + 3 + 2 + 3 + 3 = 6 odd days. 6th day after Thursday is Wednesday. Choice (B)

question.text: If 30th June, 1989 was a Friday, then what day of the week was 17th September, 1993?
question.direction: Directions for questions 16 to 35: Select the correct alternative from the given choices.

answer.explanation: Number of odd days from 30th June, 1989 to 30th June, 1993 are five. Number of days from 30th June, 1993 to 17th September, are July + August + September. Odd days: 3 + 3 + 3 = 9. Number of odd days = 9 + 5 = 14 = 0 odd days. Hence, 17th September 1993 was a Friday. Choice (C)

question.text: If 10th April, 1963 was a Wednesday, then what day of the week was 23rd August, 1959?
question.direction: Directions for questions 16 to 35: Select the correct alternative from the given choices.

answer.explanation: Number of days from 10th April, 1963 to 23rd August, 1963. Month: April + May + June + July + August. Days: 20 + 31 + 30 + 31 + 23 = 135. Number of odd days in 135 days = 135/7 = 20 days. 23rd August 1963 is 2 days to Wednesday i.e., Friday. Number of odd days from 23rd August 1963 to 23rd August 1959 are five odd days. Hence, 23rd August 1959 is five days back to Friday is Sunday. Choice (A)

question.text: If today is Sunday, then what day of the week will be the 426th day from today?
question.direction: Directions for questions 16 to 35: Select the correct alternative from the given choices.

answer.explanation: Number of odd days in 426 days = 426/7 = 60 complete weeks + 6 odd days. 6th day after Sunday is a Saturday. Choice (A)

question.text: If today is Wednesday, what day will it be, 1 year and 10 days from today?
question.direction: Directions for questions 16 to 35: Select the correct alternative from the given choices.

answer.explanation: Whether the given year is a leap year or a non-leap year, is not given, hence the answer cannot be determined. Choice (D)

question.text: In a year, if two successive months start with the same day of the week, then the year is
question.direction: Directions for questions 16 to 35: Select the correct alternative from the given choices.

answer.explanation: Two successive months can start with the same day of the week, only if the previous month does not have any odd days. This is possible only when February has 28 days. Hence, the year is a non-leap year. Choice (C)

question.text: If a year has 53 Sundays, how many Saturdays will be there in that year?
question.direction: Directions for questions 16 to 35: Select the correct alternative from the given choices.

answer.explanation: A leap year has 52 weeks and two additional days, while a non-leap year has 52 weeks and one additional day. In any year each day of the week occurs at least 52 times. A non-leap year starts and ends with the same day of the week. In a leap year the first two days of the year repeat. As it is not known whether the 53rd Sunday is the last day of the year or not, the number of Saturdays could be 52 or 53. Choice (D)

question.text: Three days ago I met my friend and asked him to lend me his maths book. He promised that he will lend it on the eighth day from that day. If today is Thursday, on which day will he lend me the book?
question.direction: Directions for questions 16 to 35: Select the correct alternative from the given choices.

answer.explanation: Today is a Thursday. Hence, the required day = Thursday − 3 (ago) + 8 (from 3 days ago) = Thursday + 5 = Tuesday. Choice (B)

question.text: There are three more days to go for my cousin to arrive. Eight days ago when I talked to him he said he would write his last exam three days later and that he would leave three days after his last exam. If his last exam is on a Saturday, on which day of the week will my cousin arrive?
question.direction: Directions for questions 16 to 35: Select the correct alternative from the given choices.

answer.explanation: Eight days ago my cousin said that his last exam is three days later i.e. five days ago from today. He is going to arrive three days later from today, i.e. eight days after the last exam. As the last exam is on a Saturday, he is arriving on a Sunday. Choice (D)

question.text: If the second Sunday of a month falls on the 8th, what is the date of the fourth day after the third Saturday of that month?
question.direction: Directions for questions 16 to 35: Select the correct alternative from the given choices.

answer.explanation: Since, 8th is the second Sunday, 7th is the first Saturday. Hence, the third Saturday is on 21st and four days later it is 25th. Choice (C)
